title: Batch versus streaming data movement
hook: Batch pipelines move data in scheduled chunks — nightly ETL, hourly aggregates. Streaming moves events continuously — fraud alerts, live dashboards. Picking the wrong model wastes money or misses the latency window.

blocks.text: Batch: AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, Step Functions scheduled workflows process data lake files on cron. Streaming: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon MSK, Kinesis Data Firehose ingest events in real time. Lambda consumers process stream records. Hybrid: Firehose batches to S3 for lake while Lambda handles hot path alerts.

blocks.text: Interview scenario: fraud needs sub-second — batch nightly fails. Daily sales report does not need Kinesis ops burden. Over-engineering streaming for monthly compliance export burns budget. Senior answer starts with latency SLA and data volume.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: ask latency SLA first. Minutes+ → batch/Glue. Sub-minute → Kinesis/MSK. Hybrid Firehose to S3 + stream consumer for alerts.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — Glue scheduled crawler and job
snippet.code:
Resources:
  EtlTrigger:
    Type: AWS::Glue::Trigger
    Properties:
      Type: SCHEDULED
      Schedule: cron(0 3 * * ? *)
      Actions:
        - JobName: !Ref DailySalesEtl
      StartOnCreation: true
  DailySalesEtl:
    Type: AWS::Glue::Job
    Properties:
      Name: daily-sales-etl
      Role: !GetAtt GlueRole.Arn
      Command:
        Name: glueetl
        ScriptLocation: s3://glue-scripts/sales_etl.py
snippet.explanation: 3 AM daily batch on data lake — appropriate for reporting SLA measured in hours.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — Firehose to S3 with Lambda transform
snippet.code:
DeliveryStream:
    Type: AWS::KinesisFirehose::DeliveryStream
    Properties:
      DeliveryStreamName: transactions-to-s3
      ExtendedS3DestinationConfiguration:
        BucketARN: !GetAtt DataLakeBucket.Arn
        Prefix: transactions/!{timestamp:yyyy/MM/dd}/
        ProcessingConfiguration:
          Enabled: true
          Processors:
            - Type: Lambda
              Parameters:
                - ParameterName: LambdaArn
                  ParameterValue: !GetAtt EnrichRecord.Arn
snippet.explanation: Firehose batches stream to S3 partitions — bridge between streaming ingest and batch analytics.

snippet.label: CLI — scale Kinesis shards before traffic spike
snippet.explanation: Each shard caps ingest — scale before Black Friday not during incident.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Kinesis for monthly report. Glue only for fraud alerts. Under-provisioned shards — throttling. No idempotent stream consumer — duplicate fraud blocks or misses.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: Kinesis IncomingRecords vs WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded. Glue job duration trend — incremental bookmark reduces batch window. Cost: Kinesis shard-month vs Glue DPU — calculate at expected volume before architecture review.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'always use Kafka.' Strong answer: latency SLA drives choice; hybrid is common; batch for lake analytics, stream for operational alerts.

interviewTakeaways: Start with latency SLA — sub-minute needs streaming; daily reports suit batch.
Kinesis shard count sets throughput ceiling — scale proactively.
Hybrid: stream for alerts, Firehose to S3, Glue for nightly aggregates.
60s: Fraud equals Kinesis Lambda. Daily report equals Glue cron. Hybrid common. Shards for throughput. Idempotent consumers.
commonPitfalls: Glue nightly for real-time fraud — misses SLA rejection.
Strong answer: Kinesis consumer with sub-second Lambda scoring.
Insufficient Kinesis shards during spike — ProvisionedThroughputExceeded.
Stream consumer without idempotency — duplicate processing.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Observable stream of events maps to Kinesis consumer; cron scheduled job maps to Glue trigger — same latency tradeoff in application code.
node-cron pulling API data hourly is batch — migrating to Kinesis when SLA tightens is common evolution path.
